newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai holds unemployment at below three pct.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai holds unemployment at below three pct.

text.p: Shanghai has found new jobs for 150,000 laid-off workers in the first nine months of 1996, keeping the city's rate of unemployment below three percent, the Liberation Daily said on Monday.
The city government and labour departments are making great efforts to find work for thousands of people losing their jobs, especially in the textile and instrument industries, it said.
Labour departments have set up more than 20 job-introduction centres and textile and instrument firms have set up retraining centres and job-referral programmes, it said.

The principal sectors that are providing new jobs include service industries, such as airlines and the city subway, as well as companies providing domestic help and shareholding companies set up by laid-off workers, it said.
Private-sector companies have hired 85,000 laid-off workers in recent years and some workers have leased land to raise pigs or grow vegetables, it said.
In the first nine months, 15,000 Shanghai people have gone to work on projects overseas, it said.
Official figures show that, as of the end of 1995, 2.7 percent of Shanghai's workforce of 4.67 million were unemployed, down from 2.8 percent a year earlier.
